On Tue, Jul 2, 2013 at 10:17 PM, Allen Benter <all...@iisys.com.au> wrote:

Hi,

I am building an interactive learning tool for statistics students using Shiny and GoogleVis.  The start can be seen at spark.rstudio.com/scm/resid/ and has, at present, two graphs showing a scatter plot and a plot of residuals.  What I would like to happen is that when one of the points in the scatter plot is selected, the corresponding point in the residual plot and the data row in the table is highlighted.  I have been able to getSelection data from the scatter plot (see spark.rstudio.com/scm/resid-old/  ) but I cannot get setSelection to work.

I have tried a simple

output$dataTable <- renderGvis({
 
    jscode <- "table.setSelection([{'row': 4}]);"
              
    temp2 <- data.frame(Data()$X, Data()$Y)
    gvisTable(temp2,
      options=list(
        gvis.listener.jscode=jscode,
        width=250, height=600
      )
    )
  })

on the table, but this does not cause the event to trigger.

Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks,

Allen

For now the package is here:
https://github.com/jcheng5/googleCharts

You can install with
if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("googleCharts", "jcheng5")

Docs are extremely sparse, but see if you can figure it out by looking at the example in inst/examples/test; the piece that's missing from there is googleSetSelection, it works but is not part of the example.

Sorry I don't have time at the moment to beef up the docs or work on another example. But give a shout if you can't figure it out.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Interactive graphs (shiny + googlevis)
parts:
Hi Andrew,

I talked to the googleVis guys during the useR conference and we intend to merge my code with their package.

For the columns parameter (which is optional), if you specify it, then you must provide a list of column() calls, one per variable in your dataframe.

I'm not familiar with motion chart options but with my bindings as they stand I think you need to have the variable you want as the id as the first variable in the data frame, and the second one is time.

If you can't figure it out, please give me a complete example I can run and I'll do my best to help. Thanks.

On Tue, Jul 16, 2013 at 11:28 AM, Andrew Clark <scott.r...@gmail.com> wrote:
Joe
  Just taking first look. Not quite sure how to handle the googleDataTable function

In a simple example
output$line <- reactive({
    
    list(
      data = googleDataTable(
        women
      )
    )
    
  })

where women only has 2 columns height and weight, I see that from
googleDataTable <- function(data, columns = NULL) etc
the columns are inferred and the chart appears as desired.

However, I have not yet succeeded in applying the columns parameter
correctly if I have a third column in the original dataset. Obviously I could subset first as an alternative

I would also like to be able to replicate a more complicated example say
the googleCharts alternative to

output$gvisMotion<- renderGvis({ gvisMotionChart(Fruits, idvar="Fruit", timevar="Year") })
where specific variables have to be assigned to idvar and timevar
Are these intended to replace the gvis Options in time? Do they have any advantages?

cheers
